<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="112.59px"/><col width="501.58px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FIFOEN</span>: FIFO mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: FIFO mode is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: FIFO mode is enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>FIFO mode can be used on standard UART communication, in SPI master/slave mode and in smartcard modes only. It must not be enabled in IrDA and LIN modes.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">M1</span>: Word length</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit must be used in conjunction with bit 12 (M0) to determine the word length. It is set or cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">M[1:0] = ‘00’: 1 start bit, 8 Data bits, n Stop bit</p><p class="TableIndent">M[1:0] = ‘01’: 1 start bit, 9 Data bits, n Stop bit</p><p class="TableIndent">M[1:0] = ‘10’: 1 start bit, 7 Data bits, n Stop bit</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In 7-bits data length mode, the smartcard mode, LIN master mode and auto baud rate (0x7F and 0x55 frames detection) are not supported.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOBIE</span>: End of Bbock interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated when the EOBF flag is set in the USART_ISR register</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTOIE</span>: Receiver timeout interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated when the RTOF bit is set in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the Receiver timeout feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 25:21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DEAT[4:0]</span>: Driver enable assertion time</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bit value defines the time between the activation of the DE (Driver Enable) signal and the beginning of the start bit. It is expressed in sample time units (1/8 or 1/16 bit time, depending on the oversampling rate). </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the Driver Enable feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 20:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DEDT[4:0]</span>: Driver enable deassertion time</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bit value defines the time between the end of the last stop bit, in a transmitted message, and the de-activation of the DE (Driver Enable) signal. It is expressed in sample time units (1/8 or 1/16 bit time, depending on the oversampling rate).</p><p class="TableIndent">If the USART_TDR register is written during the DEDT time, the new data is transmitted only when the DEDT and DEAT times have both elapsed.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the Driver Enable feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OVER8</span>: Oversampling mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Oversampling by 16</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Oversampling by 8</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In LIN, IrDA and smartcard modes, this bit must be kept cleared.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMIE</span>: Character match interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated when the CMF bit is set in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MME</span>: Mute mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the USART mute mode function. When set, the USART can switch between active and mute mode, as defined by the WAKE bit. It is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receiver in active mode permanently</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receiver can switch between mute mode and active mode. </p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">M0</span>: Word length</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used in conjunction with bit 28 (M1) to determine the word length. It is set or cleared by software (refer to bit 28 (M1)description).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WAKE</span>: Receiver wake-up method</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit determines the USART wake-up method from mute mode. It is set or cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Idle line</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Address mark</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="146.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PCE</span>: Parity control enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the hardware parity control (generation and detection). When the parity control is enabled, the computed parity is inserted at the MSB position (9th bit if M = 1; 8th bit if M = 0) and the parity is checked on the received data. This bit is set and cleared by software. Once it is set, PCE is active after the current byte (in reception and in transmission).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Parity control disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Parity control enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PS</span>: Parity selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects the odd or even parity when the parity generation/detection is enabled (PCE bit set). It is set and cleared by software. The parity is selected after the current byte.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Even parity</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Odd parity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PEIE</span>: PE interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever PE = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXEIE</span>: Transmit data register empty</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever TXE =1 in the USART_ISR register</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCIE</span>: Transmission complete interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever TC = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXNEIE</span>: Receive data register not empty</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever ORE = 1 or RXNE = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLEIE</span>: IDLE interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever IDLE = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TE</span>: Transmitter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the transmitter. It is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmitter is disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmitter is enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>During transmission, a low pulse on the TE bit (‘0’ followed by ‘1’) sends a preamble (idle line) after the current word, except in smartcard mode. In order to generate an idle character, the TE must not be immediately written to ‘1’. To ensure the required duration, the software can poll the TEACK bit in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote_">In smartcard mode, when TE is set, there is a 1 bit-time delay before the transmission starts.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RE</span>: Receiver enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the receiver. It is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receiver is disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receiver is enabled and begins searching for a start bit</p></td></tr><tr height="182.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UESM</span>: USART enable in low-power mode </p><p class="TableIndent">When this bit is cleared, the USART cannot wake up the MCU from low-power mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">When this bit is set, the USART can wake up the MCU from low-power mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: USART not able to wake up the MCU from low-power mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART able to wake up the MCU from low-power mode. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>It is recommended to set the UESM bit just before entering low-power mode and clear it when exit from low-power mode. </p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="212.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UE</span>: USART enable</p><p class="TableIndent">When this bit is cleared, the USART prescalers and outputs are stopped immediately, and all current operations are discarded. The USART configuration is kept, but all the USART_ISR status flags are reset. This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: USART prescaler and outputs disabled, low-power mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>To enter low-power mode without generating errors on the line, the TE bit must be previously reset and the software must wait for the TC bit in the USART_ISR to be set before resetting the UE bit. </p><p class="RegTNote_">The DMA requests are also reset when UE = 0 so the DMA channel must be disabled before resetting the UE bit.</p><p class="RegTNote_">In smartcard mode, (SCEN = 1), the CK pin is always available when CLKEN = 1, regardless of the UE bit value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.3 USART control register 2 (USART\_CR2)

Address offset: 0x04

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="80.09px"/><col width="534.50px"/><tr height="269.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ADD[7:0]</span>: Address of the USART node </p><p class="TableIndent">These bits give the address of the USART node in mute mode or a character code to be recognized in low-power or Run mode:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>In mute mode: they are used in multiprocessor communication to wake up from mute mode with 4-bit/7-bit address mark detection. The MSB of the character sent by the transmitter should be equal to 1. In 4-bit address mark detection, only ADD[3:0] bits are used.</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>In low-power mode: they are used for wake up from low-power mode on character match.<br/>When WUS[1:0] is programmed to 0b00 (WUF active on address match), the wake-up from low-power mode is performed when the received character corresponds to the character programmed through ADD[6:0] or ADD[3:0] bitfield (depending on ADDM7 bit), and WUF interrupt is enabled by setting WUFIE bit. <span style="font-kerning:none;">The MSB of the character sent by transmitter should be equal to 1.</span></p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>In Run mode with mute mode inactive (for example, end-of-block detection in ModBus protocol): the whole received character (8 bits) is compared to ADD[7:0] value and CMF flag is set on match. An interrupt is generated if the CMIE bit is set.</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits can only be written when the reception is disabled (RE = 0) or when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTOEN</span>: Receiver timeout enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receiver timeout feature disabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receiver timeout feature enabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">When this feature is enabled, the RTOF flag in the USART_ISR register is set if the RX line is idle (no reception) for the duration programmed in the RTOR (receiver timeout register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the Receiver timeout feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="198.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRMOD[1:0]</span>: Auto baud rate mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Measurement of the start bit is used to detect the baud rate. </p><p class="TableIndent">01: Falling edge to falling edge measurement (the received frame must start with a single bit = 1 and Frame = Start10xxxxxx)</p><p class="TableIndent">10: 0x7F frame detection.</p><p class="TableIndent">11: 0x55 frame detection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when ABREN = 0 or the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If DATAINV<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1 and/or MSBFIRST<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1 the patterns must be the same on the line, for example 0xAA for MSBFIRST)</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABREN</span>: Auto baud rate enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Auto baud rate detection is disabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Auto baud rate detection is enabled. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MSBFIRST</span>: Most significant bit first</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: data is transmitted/received with data bit 0 first, following the start bit. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: data is transmitted/received with the MSB (bit 7/8) first, following the start bit. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DATAINV: </span>Binary data inversion</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Logical data from the data register are send/received in positive/direct logic. (1 = H, 0 = L) </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Logical data from the data register are send/received in negative/inverse logic. (1 = L, 0 = H). The parity bit is also inverted.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXINV: </span>TX pin active level inversion</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TX pin signal works using the standard logic levels (V<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DD</span></sub> =1/idle, Gnd = 0/mark) </p><p class="TableIndent">1: TX pin signal values are inverted (V<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DD</span></sub> =0/mark, Gnd = 1/idle). </p><p class="TableIndent">This enables the use of an external inverter on the TX line. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXINV: </span>RX pin active level inversion</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: RX pin signal works using the standard logic levels (V<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DD</span></sub> =1/idle, Gnd = 0/mark) </p><p class="TableIndent">1: RX pin signal values are inverted (V<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DD</span></sub> =0/mark, Gnd = 1/idle). </p><p class="TableIndent">This enables the use of an external inverter on the RX line. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SWAP: </span>Swap TX/RX pins</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TX/RX pins are used as defined in standard pinout</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The TX and RX pins functions are swapped. This enables to work in the case of a cross-wired connection to another UART. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LINEN</span>: LIN mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LIN mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: LIN mode enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">The LIN mode enables the capability to send LIN synchronous breaks (13 low bits) using the SBKRQ bit in the USART_CR1 register, and to detect LIN Sync breaks.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support LIN mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">STOP[1:0]</span>: Stop bits</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are used for programming the stop bits.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: 1 stop bit</p><p class="TableIndent">01: 0.5 stop bit.</p><p class="TableIndent">10: 2 stop bits</p><p class="TableIndent">11: 1.5 stop bits</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="225.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CLKEN</span>: Clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the user to enable the CK pin.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CK pin disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CK pin enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If neither synchronous mode nor smartcard mode is supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p><p class="RegTNote_">In smartcard mode, in order to provide correctly the CK clock to the smartcard, the steps below must be respected:<br/>UE = 0<br/>SCEN = 1<br/>GTPR configuration<br/>CLKEN= 1<br/>UE = 1</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPOL</span>: Clock polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the user to select the polarity of the clock output on the CK pin in synchronous mode. It works in conjunction with the CPHA bit to produce the desired clock/data relationship </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Steady low value on CK pin outside transmission window</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Steady high value on CK pin outside transmission window</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If synchronous mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="149.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CPHA</span>: Clock phase</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used to select the phase of the clock output on the CK pin in synchronous mode. It works in conjunction with the CPOL bit to produce the desired clock/data relationship (see <a href="#XREF_81699__Figure_6__Data_sampling_for_noise_detection_(bit_OVER8_=_0)24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 570</a> and <a href="#XREF_32354__Figure_7__Data_sampling_when_oversampling_by_824" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 571</a>)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The first clock transition is the first data capture edge</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The second clock transition is the first data capture edge</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If synchronous mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="170.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBCL</span>: Last bit clock pulse</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used to select whether the clock pulse associated with the last data bit transmitted (MSB) has to be output on the CK pin in synchronous mode. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: The clock pulse of the last data bit is not output to the CK pin</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The clock pulse of the last data bit is output to the CK pin</p><p class="RegTCaution"><span class="Bold">Caution:<span style="padding-right:8pt ;">​</span></span>The last bit is the 7th or 8th or 9th data bit transmitted depending on the 7 or 8 or 9 bit format selected by the M bit in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If synchronous mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBDIE</span>: LIN break detection interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Break interrupt mask (break detection using break delimiter).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt is inhibited<br/>1: An interrupt is generated whenever LBDF = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If LIN mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBDL</span>: LIN<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>break detection length</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is for selection between 11 bit or 10 bit break detection.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: 10-bit break detection</p><p class="TableIndent">1: 11-bit break detection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If LIN mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ADDM7</span>: 7-bit address detection/4-bit address detection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is for selection between 4-bit address detection or 7-bit address detection. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: 4-bit address detection</p><p class="TableIndent">1: 7-bit address detection (in 8-bit data mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In 7-bit and 9-bit data modes, the address detection is done on 6-bit and 8-bit address (ADD[5:0] and ADD[7:0]) respectively.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-weight:Bold;">DIS_NSS<span style="font-weight:normal;">: NSS pin enable</span></p><p class="TableIndent">When the DIS_NSS bit is set, the NSS pin input is ignored.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: SPI slave selection depends on NSS input pin.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: SPI slave is always selected and NSS input pin is ignored.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When SPI slave mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SLVEN</span>: Synchronous slave mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">When the SLVEN bit is set, the synchronous slave mode is enabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Slave mode disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Slave mode enabled.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When SPI slave mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>. </p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

The CPOL, CPHA and LBCL bits should not be written while the transmitter is enabled.

### 40.8.4 USART control register 3 (USART\_CR3)

Address offset: 0x08

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="116.36px"/><col width="494.50px"/><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFTCFG[2:0]: </span>TXFIFO threshold configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">000:TXFIFO reaches 1/8 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">001:TXFIFO reaches 1/4 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">010:TXFIFO reaches 1/2 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">011:TXFIFO reaches 3/4 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">100:TXFIFO reaches 7/8 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">101:TXFIFO becomes empty</p><p class="TableIndent">Remaining combinations: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFTIE</span>: RXFIFO threshold interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated when Receive FIFO reaches the threshold programmed in RXFTCFG.</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 27:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFTCFG[2:0]: </span>Receive FIFO threshold configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">000:Receive FIFO reaches 1/8 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">001:Receive FIFO reaches 1/4 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">010:Receive FIFO reaches 1/2 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">011:Receive FIFO reaches 3/4 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">100:Receive FIFO reaches 7/8 of its depth</p><p class="TableIndent">101:Receive FIFO becomes full</p><p class="TableIndent">Remaining combinations: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCBGTIE</span>: Transmission complete before guard time, interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever TCBGT=1 in the USART_ISR register</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFTIE</span>: TXFIFO threshold interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated when TXFIFO reaches the threshold programmed in TXFTCFG.</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WUFIE</span>: Wake-up from low-power mode interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: USART interrupt generated whenever WUF = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>WUFIE must be set before entering in low-power mode.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="181.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WUS[1:0]</span>: Wake-up from low-power mode interrupt flag selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield specifies the event which activates the WUF (wake-up from low-power mode flag). </p><p class="TableIndent">00: WUF active on address match (as defined by ADD[7:0] and ADDM7)</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Reserved.</p><p class="TableIndent">10: WUF active on start bit detection</p><p class="TableIndent">11: WUF active on RXNE/RXFNE. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="226.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SCARCNT[2:0]</span>: Smartcard auto-retry count</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield specifies the number of retries for transmission and reception in smartcard mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">In transmission mode, it specifies the number of automatic retransmission retries, before generating a transmission error (FE bit set).</p><p class="TableIndent">In reception mode, it specifies the number or erroneous reception trials, before generating a reception error (RXNE/RXFNE and PE bits set).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield must be programmed only when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="TableIndent">When the USART is enabled (UE = 1), this bitfield may only be written to 0x0, in order to stop retransmission. </p><p class="TableIndent">0x0: retransmission disabled - No automatic retransmission in transmit mode. </p><p class="TableIndent">0x1 to 0x7: number of automatic retransmission attempts (before signaling error)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If smartcard mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DEP</span>: Driver enable polarity selection</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DE signal is active high. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: DE signal is active low.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the Driver Enable feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DEM</span>: Driver enable mode </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the user to activate the external transceiver control, through the DE signal. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: DE function is disabled. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: DE function is enabled. The DE signal is output on the RTS pin.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the Driver Enable feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="177.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DDRE</span>: DMA Disable on reception error</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA is not disabled in case of reception error. The corresponding error flag is set but RXNE is kept 0 preventing from overrun. As a consequence, the DMA request is not asserted, so the erroneous data is not transferred (no DMA request), but next correct received data is transferred (used for smartcard mode).</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA is disabled following a reception error. The corresponding error flag is set, as well as RXNE. The DMA request is masked until the error flag is cleared. This means that the software must first disable the DMA request (DMAR = 0) or clear RXNE/RXFNE is case FIFO mode is enabled) before clearing the error flag.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE=0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The reception errors are: parity error, framing error or noise error.</p></td></tr><tr height="180.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OVRDIS</span>: Overrun disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used to disable the receive overrun detection. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Overrun Error Flag, ORE, is set when received data is not read before receiving new data. </p><p class="TableIndent">1: Overrun functionality is disabled. If new data is received while the RXNE flag is still set</p><p class="TableIndent">the ORE flag is not set and the new received data overwrites the previous content of the USART_RDR register. When FIFO mode is enabled, the RXFIFO is bypassed and data is written directly in USART_RDR register. Even when FIFO management is enabled, the RXNE flag is to be used.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This control bit enables checking the communication flow w/o reading the data</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ONEBIT</span>: One sample bit method enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the user to select the sample method. When the one sample bit method is selected the noise detection flag (NE) is disabled.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Three sample bit method</p><p class="TableIndent">1: One sample bit method</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTSIE</span>: CTS interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt is inhibited<br/>1: An interrupt is generated whenever CTSIF = 1 in the USART_ISR register</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTSE</span>: CTS enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CTS hardware flow control disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CTS mode enabled, data is only transmitted when the CTS input is deasserted (tied to 0). If the CTS input is asserted while data is being transmitted, then the transmission is completed before stopping. If data is written into the data register while CTS is asserted, the transmission is postponed until CTS is deasserted.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTSE</span>: RTS enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: RTS hardware flow control disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: RTS output enabled, data is only requested when there is space in the receive buffer. The transmission of data is expected to cease after the current character has been transmitted. The RTS output is deasserted (pulled to 0) when data can be received.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAT</span>: DMA enable transmitter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by software</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA mode is enabled for transmission</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA mode is disabled for transmission</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAR</span>: DMA enable receiver</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by software</p><p class="TableIndent">1: DMA mode is enabled for reception</p><p class="TableIndent">0: DMA mode is disabled for reception</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SCEN</span>: Smartcard mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used for enabling smartcard mode.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Smartcard mode disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Smartcard mode enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">NACK</span>: Smartcard NACK enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: NACK transmission in case of parity error is disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: NACK transmission during parity error is enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">HDSEL</span>: Half-duplex selection</p><p class="TableIndent">Selection of single-wire half-duplex mode </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Half duplex mode is not selected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Half duplex mode is selected </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IRLP</span>: IrDA low-power</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used for selecting between normal and low-power IrDA modes</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Normal mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Low-power mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If IrDA mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IREN</span>: IrDA mode enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: IrDA disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: IrDA enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If IrDA mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EIE</span>: Error interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">Error Interrupt Enable Bit is required to enable interrupt generation in case of a framing error, overrun error noise flag or SPI slave underrun error (FE = 1 or ORE = 1 or NE = 1 or UDR = 1 in the USART_ISR register).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt inhibited</p><p class="TableIndent">1: interrupt generated when FE = 1 or ORE = 1 or NE = 1 or UDR = 1 (in SPI slave mode) in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.5 USART baud rate register (USART\_BRR)

This register can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0). It may be automatically updated by hardware in auto baud rate detection mode.

Address offset: 0x0C

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.54px"/><col width="498.31px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GT[7:0]</span>: Guard time value</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is used to program the Guard time value in terms of number of baud clock periods. </p><p class="TableIndent">This is used in smartcard mode. The Transmission Complete flag is set after this guard time value.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If smartcard mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="420.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PSC[7:0]</span>: Prescaler value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">In IrDA low-power and normal IrDA mode:</span></p><p class="TableIndent">PSC[7:0] = IrDA normal and low-power baud rate</p><p class="TableIndent">PSC[7:0] is used to program the prescaler for dividing the USART source clock to achieve the low-power frequency: the source clock is divided by the value given in the register (8 significant bits):</p><p class="TableIndent" style="font-weight:Bold;">In smartcard mode:</p><p class="TableIndent">PSC[4:0] = Prescaler value</p><p class="TableIndent">PSC[4:0] is used to program the prescaler for dividing the USART source clock to provide the smartcard clock. The value given in the register (5 significant bits) is multiplied by 2 to give the division factor of the source clock frequency:</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableIndent">00000: Reserved - do not program this value</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 55.38pt;">00001: Divides the source clock by 1 (IrDA mode) / by 2 (smartcard mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">00010: Divides the source clock by 2 (IrDA mode) / by 4 (smartcard mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">00011: Divides the source clock by 3 (IrDA mode) / by 6 (smartcard mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">11111: Divides the source clock by 31 (IrDA mode) / by 62 (smartcard mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">0010 0000: Divides the source clock by 32 (IrDA mode)</p><p class="TableIndent">...</p><p class="TableIndent">1111 1111: Divides the source clock by 255 (IrDA mode)</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Bits [7:5] must be kept cleared if smartcard mode is used.</p><p class="RegTNote_">This bitfield is reserved and forced by hardware to ‘0’ when the smartcard and IrDA modes are not supported. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.7 USART receiver timeout register (USART\_RTOR)

Address offset: 0x14

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.54px"/><col width="498.31px"/><tr height="226.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BLEN[7:0]</span>: Block length </p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield gives the Block length in smartcard T = 1 Reception. Its value equals the number of information characters + the length of the Epilogue Field (1-LEC/2-CRC) - 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">Examples: </p><p class="TableIndent">BLEN = 0: 0 information characters + LEC</p><p class="TableIndent">BLEN = 1: 0 information characters + CRC</p><p class="TableIndent">BLEN = 255: 254 information characters + CRC (total 256 characters))</p><p class="TableIndent">In smartcard mode, the Block length counter is reset when TXE = 0 (TXFE = 0 in case FIFO mode is enabled).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield can be used also in other modes. In this case, the Block length counter is reset when RE = 0 (receiver disabled) and/or when the EOBCF bit is written to 1. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This value can be programmed after the start of the block reception (using the data from the LEN character in the Prologue Field). It must be programmed only once per received block. </p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTO[23:0]</span>: Receiver timeout value</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield gives the Receiver timeout value in terms of number of bits during which there is no activity on the RX line.</p><p class="TableIndent">In standard mode, the RTOF flag is set if, after the last received character, no new start bit is detected for more than the RTO value.</p><p class="TableIndent">In smartcard mode, this value is used to implement the CWT and BWT. See smartcard chapter for more details. In the standard, the CWT/BWT measurement is done starting from the start bit of the last received character.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This value must only be programmed once per received character. </p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

RTOR can be written on-the-fly. If the new value is lower than or equal to the counter, the RTOF flag is set.

This register is reserved and forced by hardware to “0x00000000” when the Receiver timeout feature is not supported. Refer to [Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691](#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24).

### 40.8.8 USART request register (USART\_RQR)

Address offset: 0x18

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.54px"/><col width="495.86px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="176.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFRQ</span>: Transmit data flush request</p><p class="TableIndent">When FIFO mode is disabled, writing ‘1’ to this bit sets the TXE flag. This enables to discard the transmit data. This bit must be used only in smartcard mode, when data have not been sent due to errors (NACK) and the FE flag is active in the USART_ISR register. If the USART does not support smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value.</p><p class="TableIndent">When FIFO is enabled, TXFRQ bit is set to flush the whole FIFO. This sets the TXFE flag (Transmit FIFO empty, bit 23 in the USART_ISR register). Flushing the Transmit FIFO is supported in both UART and smartcard modes. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In FIFO mode, the TXFNF flag is reset during the flush request until TxFIFO is empty in order to ensure that no data are written in the data register.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFRQ</span>: Receive data flush request</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit empties the entire receive FIFO i.e. clears the bit RXFNE.</p><p class="TableIndent">This enables to discard the received data without reading them, and avoid an overrun condition.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MMRQ</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Mute mode request</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit puts the USART in mute mode and resets the RWU flag.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SBKRQ</span>: Send break request</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit sets the SBKF flag and request to send a BREAK on the line, as soon as the transmit machine is available.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When the application needs to send the break character following all previously inserted data, including the ones not yet transmitted, the software should wait for the TXE flag assertion before setting the SBKRQ bit.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRRQ</span>: Auto baud rate request</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit resets the ABRF and ABRE flags in the USART_ISR and requests an automatic baud rate measurement on the next received data frame. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.9 USART interrupt and status register (USART\_ISR)

Address offset: 0x1C

Reset value: 0x0X80 00C0

X = 2 if FIFO/smartcard mode is enabled

X = 0 if FIFO is enabled and smartcard mode is disabled

The same register can be used in FIFO mode enabled (this section) and FIFO mode disabled (next section).

FIFO mode enabled
