<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.54px"/><col width="495.86px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFT</span>: TXFIFO threshold flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the TXFIFO reaches the threshold programmed in TXFTCFG of USART_CR3 register i.e. the TXFIFO contains TXFTCFG empty locations. An interrupt is generated if the TXFTIE bit  = 1 (bit 31) in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: TXFIFO does not reach the programmed threshold.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: TXFIFO reached the programmed threshold.</p></td></tr><tr height="177.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFT</span>: RXFIFO threshold flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the threshold programmed in RXFTCFG in USART_CR3 register is reached. This means that there are (RXFTCFG - 1) data in the Receive FIFO and one data in the USART_RDR register. An interrupt is generated if the RXFTIE bit  = 1 (bit 27) in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receive FIFO does not reach the programmed threshold.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receive FIFO reached the programmed threshold.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When the RXFTCFG threshold is configured to ‘101’, RXFT flag is set if 16 data are available i.e. 15 data in the RXFIFO and 1 data in the USART_RDR. Consequently, the 17th received data does not cause an overrun error. The overrun error occurs after receiving the 18th data.</p></td></tr><tr height="253.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCBGT: </span>Transmission complete before guard time flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set when the last data written in the USART_TDR has been transmitted correctly out of the shift register. </p><p class="TableIndent">It is set by hardware in smartcard mode, if the transmission of a frame containing data is complete and if the smartcard did not send back any NACK. An interrupt is generated if TCBGTIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the TCBGTCF in the USART_ICR register or by a write to the USART_TDR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmission is not complete or transmission is complete unsuccessfully (i.e. a NACK is received from the card)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission is complete successfully (before Guard time completion and there is no NACK from the smart card).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. If the USART supports the smartcard mode and the smartcard mode is enabled, the TCBGT reset value is ‘1’. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFF</span>: RXFIFO full</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the number of received data corresponds to RXFIFO size + 1 (RXFIFO full + 1 data in the USART_RDR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the RXFFIE bit  = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: RXFIFO not full.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: RXFIFO Full.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFE</span>: TXFIFO empty</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when TXFIFO is empty. When the TXFIFO contains at least one data, this flag is cleared. The TXFE flag can also be set by writing 1 to the bit TXFRQ (bit 4) in the USART_RQR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the TXFEIE bit  = 1 (bit 30) in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: TXFIFO not empty.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: TXFIFO empty.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REACK</span>: Receive enable acknowledge flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware, when the Receive Enable value is taken into account by the USART. </p><p class="TableIndent">It can be used to verify that the USART is ready for reception before entering low-power mode.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEACK</span>: Transmit enable acknowledge flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware, when the Transmit Enable value is taken into account by the USART. </p><p class="TableIndent">It can be used when an idle frame request is generated by writing TE = 0, followed by TE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register, in order to respect the TE = 0 minimum period. </p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WUF</span>: Wake-up from low-power mode flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware, when a wake-up event is detected. The event is defined by the WUS bitfield. It is cleared by software, writing a 1 to the WUCF in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if WUFIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When UESM is cleared, WUF flag is also cleared.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="164.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RWU</span>: Receiver wake-up from mute mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates if the USART is in mute mode. It is cleared/set by hardware when a wake-up/mute sequence is recognized. The mute mode control sequence (address or IDLE) is selected by the WAKE bit in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When wake-up on IDLE mode is selected, this bit can only be set by software, writing 1 to the MMRQ bit in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receiver in active mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receiver in mute mode</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SBKF</span>: Send break flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates that a send break character was requested. It is set by software, by writing 1 to the SBKRQ bit in the USART_CR3 register. It is automatically reset by hardware during the stop bit of break transmission.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break character transmitted</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Break character requested by setting SBKRQ bit in USART_RQR register</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMF</span>: Character match flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware, when a the character defined by ADD[7:0] is received. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the CMCF in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if CMIE = 1in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Character match detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Character Match detected</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BUSY</span>: Busy flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and reset by hardware. It is active when a communication is ongoing on the RX line (successful start bit detected). It is reset at the end of the reception (successful or not). </p><p class="TableIndent">0: USART is idle (no reception)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reception on going</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRF:</span> Auto baud rate flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the automatic baud rate has been set (RXFNE is also set, generating an interrupt if RXFNEIE = 1) or when the auto baud rate operation was completed without success (ABRE = 1) (ABRE, RXFNE and FE are also set in this case)</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, in order to request a new auto baud rate detection, by writing 1 to the ABRRQ in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRE</span>: Auto baud rate error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware if the baud rate measurement failed (baud rate out of range or character comparison failed)</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the ABRRQ bit in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDR</span>: SPI slave underrun error flag</p><p class="TableIndent">In slave transmission mode, this flag is set when the first clock pulse for data transmission appears while the software has not yet loaded any value into USART_TDR. This flag is reset by setting UDRCF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No underrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: underrun error</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the SPI slave mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOBF</span>: End of block flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a complete block has been received (for example T = 1 smartcard mode). The detection is done when the number of received bytes (from the start of the block, including the prologue) is equal or greater than BLEN + 4.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the EOBIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the EOBCF in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: End of Block not reached</p><p class="TableIndent">1: End of Block (number of characters) reached</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If smartcard mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="242.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTOF</span>: Receiver timeout</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timeout value, programmed in the RTOR register has lapsed, without any communication. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the RTOCF bit in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RTOIE = 1 in the USART_CR2 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">In smartcard mode, the timeout corresponds to the CWT or BWT timings.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Timeout value not reached<br/>1: Timeout value reached without any data reception</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If a time equal to the value programmed in RTOR register separates 2 characters, RTOF is not set. If this time exceeds this value + 2 sample times (2/16 or 2/8, depending on the oversampling method), RTOF flag is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The counter counts even if RE = 0 but RTOF is set only when RE = 1. If the timeout has already elapsed when RE is set, then RTOF is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the Receiver timeout feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTS</span>: CTS flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware. It is an inverted copy of the status of the CTS input pin. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: CTS line set</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CTS line reset</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTSIF</span>: CTS interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the CTS input toggles, if the CTSE bit is set. It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the CTSCF bit in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if CTSIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No change occurred on the CTS status line</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A change occurred on the CTS status line</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBDF</span>: LIN break detection flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the LIN break is detected. It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the LBDCF in the USART_ICR. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if LBDIE = 1 in the USART_CR2 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LIN Break not detected<br/>1: LIN break detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support LIN mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="196.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFNF: </span>TXFIFO not full</p><p class="TableIndent">TXFNF is set by hardware when TXFIFO is not full meaning that data can be written in the USART_TDR. Every write operation to the USART_TDR places the data in the TXFIFO. This flag remains set until the TXFIFO is full. When the TXFIFO is full, this flag is cleared indicating that data can not be written into the USART_TDR. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the TXFNFIE bit =1 in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmit FIFO is full</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmit FIFO is not full</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The TXFNF is kept reset during the flush request until TXFIFO is empty. After sending the flush request (by setting TXFRQ bit), the flag TXFNF should be checked prior to writing in TXFIFO (TXFNF and TXFE are set at the same time).</p><p class="RegTNote_">This bit is used during single buffer transmission.</p></td></tr><tr height="181.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TC</span>: Transmission complete</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates that the last data written in the USART_TDR has been transmitted out of the shift register.</p><p class="TableIndent">It is set by hardware when the transmission of a frame containing data is complete and when TXFE is set. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if TCIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">TC bit is is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the TCCF in the USART_ICR register or by a write to the USART_TDR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmission is not complete</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission is complete</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If TE bit is reset and no transmission is on going, the TC bit is immediately set.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXFNE</span>: RXFIFO not empty</p><p class="TableIndent">RXFNE bit is set by hardware when the RXFIFO is not empty, meaning that data can be read from the USART_RDR register. Every read operation from the USART_RDR frees a location in the RXFIFO. </p><p class="TableIndent">RXFNE is cleared when the RXFIFO is empty. The RXFNE flag can also be cleared by writing 1 to the RXFRQ in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RXFNEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Data is not received</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Received data is ready to be read.</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLE</span>: Idle line detected</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when an Idle Line is detected. An interrupt is generated if IDLEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the IDLECF in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Idle line is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Idle line is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The IDLE bit is not set again until the RXFNE bit has been set (i.e. a new idle line occurs).</p><p class="RegTNote_">If mute mode is enabled (MME<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1), IDLE is set if the USART is not mute (RWU<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>0), whatever the mute mode selected by the WAKE bit. If RWU<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1, IDLE is not set.</p></td></tr><tr height="212.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ORE</span>: Overrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the data currently being received in the shift register is</p><p class="TableIndent">ready to be transferred into the USART_RDR register while RXFF = 1. It is cleared by a software, writing 1 to the ORECF, in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RXFNEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register, or EIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No overrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Overrun error is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When this bit is set, the USART_RDR register content is not lost but the shift register is overwritten. An interrupt is generated if the ORE flag is set during multi buffer communication if the EIE bit is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">This bit is permanently forced to 0 (no overrun detection) when the bit OVRDIS is set in the USART_CR3 register.</p></td></tr><tr height="197.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">NE</span>: Noise detection flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when noise is detected on a received frame. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the NECF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No noise is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Noise is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit does not generate an interrupt as it appears at the same time as the RXFNE bit which itself generates an interrupt. An interrupt is generated when the NE flag is set during multi buffer communication if the EIE bit is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">When the line is noise-free, the NE flag can be disabled by programming the ONEBIT bit to 1 to increase the USART tolerance to deviations (Refer to <a href="#XREF_19021__1_3_5_USART_clock_tolerance24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.5.8: Tolerance of the USART receiver to clock deviation on page 1708</a>).</p><p class="RegTNote_">This error is associated with the character in the USART_RDR.</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FE</span>: Framing error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a de-synchronization, excessive noise or a break character is detected. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the FECF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When transmitting data in smartcard mode, this bit is set when the maximum number of transmit attempts is reached without success (the card NACKs the data frame).</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if EIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Framing error is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Framing error or break character is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This error is associated with the character in the USART_RDR.</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PE</span>: Parity error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a parity error occurs in receiver mode. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the PECF in the USART_ICR register. <br/>An interrupt is generated if PEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No parity error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Parity error</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This error is associated with the character in the USART_RDR.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.10 USART interrupt and status register [alternate] (USART\_ISR)

Address offset: 0x1C

Reset value: 0x0000 00C0

The same register can be used in FIFO mode enabled (previous section) and FIFO mode disabled (this section).

FIFO mode disabled

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.54px"/><col width="495.86px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="253.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCBGT: </span>Transmission complete before guard time flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set when the last data written in the USART_TDR has been transmitted correctly out of the shift register. </p><p class="TableIndent">It is set by hardware in smartcard mode, if the transmission of a frame containing data is complete and if the smartcard did not send back any NACK. An interrupt is generated if TCBGTIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the TCBGTCF in the USART_ICR register or by a write to the USART_TDR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmission is not complete or transmission is complete unsuccessfully (i.e. a NACK is received from the card)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission is complete successfully (before Guard time completion and there is no NACK from the smart card).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. If the USART supports the smartcard mode and the smartcard mode is enabled, the TCBGT reset value is ‘1’. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24:23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REACK</span>: Receive enable acknowledge flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware, when the Receive Enable value is taken into account by the USART. </p><p class="TableIndent">It can be used to verify that the USART is ready for reception before entering low-power mode.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEACK</span>: Transmit enable acknowledge flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware, when the Transmit Enable value is taken into account by the USART. </p><p class="TableIndent">It can be used when an idle frame request is generated by writing TE = 0, followed by TE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register, in order to respect the TE = 0 minimum period. </p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WUF</span>: Wake-up from low-power mode flag </p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware, when a wake-up event is detected. The event is defined by the WUS bitfield. It is cleared by software, writing a 1 to the WUCF in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if WUFIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When UESM is cleared, WUF flag is also cleared.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="164.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RWU</span>: <span style="font-style:Italic;">Receiver wake-up from mute mode</span></p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates if the USART is in mute mode. It is cleared/set by hardware when a wake-up/mute sequence is recognized. The mute mode control sequence (address or IDLE) is selected by the WAKE bit in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When wake-up on IDLE mode is selected, this bit can only be set by software, writing 1 to the MMRQ bit in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Receiver in active mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Receiver in mute mode</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SBKF</span>: Send break flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates that a send break character was requested. It is set by software, by writing 1 to the SBKRQ bit in the USART_CR3 register. It is automatically reset by hardware during the stop bit of break transmission.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break character transmitted</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Break character requested by setting SBKRQ bit in USART_RQR register</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMF</span>: Character match flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware, when a the character defined by ADD[7:0] is received. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the CMCF in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if CMIE = 1in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Character match detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Character Match detected</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BUSY</span>: Busy flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and reset by hardware. It is active when a communication is ongoing on the RX line (successful start bit detected). It is reset at the end of the reception (successful or not). </p><p class="TableIndent">0: USART is idle (no reception)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reception on going</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRF:</span> Auto baud rate flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the automatic baud rate has been set (RXNE is also set, generating an interrupt if RXNEIE = 1) or when the auto baud rate operation was completed without success (ABRE = 1) (ABRE, RXNE and FE are also set in this case)</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, in order to request a new auto baud rate detection, by writing 1 to the ABRRQ in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ABRE</span>: Auto baud rate error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware if the baud rate measurement failed (baud rate out of range or character comparison failed)</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the ABRRQ bit in the USART_RQR register. </p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the auto baud rate feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDR</span>: SPI slave underrun error flag</p><p class="TableIndent">In slave transmission mode, this flag is set when the first clock pulse for data transmission appears while the software has not yet loaded any value into USART_TDR. This flag is reset by setting UDRCF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No underrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: underrun error</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the SPI slave mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOBF</span>: End of block flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a complete block has been received (for example T = 1 smartcard mode). The detection is done when the number of received bytes (from the start of the block, including the prologue) is equal or greater than BLEN + 4.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the EOBIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the EOBCF in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: End of Block not reached</p><p class="TableIndent">1: End of Block (number of characters) reached</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If smartcard mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="242.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTOF</span>: Receiver timeout</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the timeout value, programmed in the RTOR register has lapsed, without any communication. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the RTOCF bit in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RTOIE = 1 in the USART_CR2 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">In smartcard mode, the timeout corresponds to the CWT or BWT timings.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Timeout value not reached<br/>1: Timeout value reached without any data reception</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If a time equal to the value programmed in RTOR register separates 2 characters, RTOF is not set. If this time exceeds this value + 2 sample times (2/16 or 2/8, depending on the oversampling method), RTOF flag is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">The counter counts even if RE = 0 but RTOF is set only when RE = 1. If the timeout has already elapsed when RE is set, then RTOF is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the USART does not support the Receiver timeout feature, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTS</span>: CTS flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set/reset by hardware. It is an inverted copy of the status of the CTS input pin. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: CTS line set</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CTS line reset</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTSIF</span>: CTS interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the CTS input toggles, if the CTSE bit is set. It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the CTSCF bit in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if CTSIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No change occurred on the CTS status line</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A change occurred on the CTS status line</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBDF</span>: LIN break detection flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the LIN break is detected. It is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the LBDCF in the USART_ICR. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if LBDIE = 1 in the USART_CR2 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: LIN Break not detected<br/>1: LIN break detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support LIN mode, this bit is reserved and kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXE: </span>Transmit data register empty</p><p class="TableIndent">TXE is set by hardware when the content of the USART_TDR register has been transferred into the shift register. It is cleared by writing to the USART_TDR register. The TXE flag can also be set by writing 1 to the TXFRQ in the USART_RQR register, in order to discard the data (only in smartcard T = 0 mode, in case of transmission failure).</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if the TXEIE bit  = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Data register full</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Data register not full</p></td></tr><tr height="181.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TC</span>: Transmission complete</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit indicates that the last data written in the USART_TDR has been transmitted out of the shift register.</p><p class="TableIndent">It is set by hardware when the transmission of a frame containing data is complete and when TXE is set. </p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if TCIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. </p><p class="TableIndent">TC bit is is cleared by software, by writing 1 to the TCCF in the USART_ICR register or by a write to the USART_TDR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Transmission is not complete</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission is complete</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If TE bit is reset and no transmission is on going, the TC bit is set immediately.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RXNE</span>: Read data register not empty</p><p class="TableIndent">RXNE bit is set by hardware when the content of the USART_RDR shift register has been transferred to the USART_RDR register. It is cleared by reading from the USART_RDR register. The RXNE flag can also be cleared by writing 1 to the RXFRQ in the USART_RQR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RXNEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Data is not received</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Received data is ready to be read.</p></td></tr><tr height="165.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLE</span>: Idle line detected</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when an Idle Line is detected. An interrupt is generated if IDLEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the IDLECF in the USART_ICR register. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Idle line is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Idle line is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The IDLE bit is not set again until the RXNE bit has been set (i.e. a new idle line occurs).</p><p class="RegTNote_">If mute mode is enabled (MME<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1), IDLE is set if the USART is not mute (RWU<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>0), whatever the mute mode selected by the WAKE bit. If RWU<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1, IDLE is not set.</p></td></tr><tr height="228.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ORE</span>: Overrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when the data currently being received in the shift register is</p><p class="TableIndent">ready to be transferred into the USART_RDR register while RXNE = 1. It is cleared by a software, writing 1 to the ORECF, in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if RXNEIE = 1 or EIE  =  1 in the LPUART_CR1 register, or EIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableIndent">0: No overrun error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Overrun error is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When this bit is set, the USART_RDR register content is not lost but the shift register is overwritten. An interrupt is generated if the ORE flag is set during multi buffer communication if the EIE bit is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">This bit is permanently forced to 0 (no overrun detection) when the bit OVRDIS is set in the USART_CR3 register.</p></td></tr><tr height="180.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">NE</span>: Noise detection flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when noise is detected on a received frame. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the NECF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No noise is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Noise is detected</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit does not generate an interrupt as it appears at the same time as the RXNE bit which itself generates an interrupt. An interrupt is generated when the NE flag is set during multi buffer communication if the EIE bit is set.</p><p class="RegTNote_">When the line is noise-free, the NE flag can be disabled by programming the ONEBIT bit to 1 to increase the USART tolerance to deviations (Refer to <a href="#XREF_19021__1_3_5_USART_clock_tolerance24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.5.8: Tolerance of the USART receiver to clock deviation on page 1708</a>).</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FE</span>: Framing error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a de-synchronization, excessive noise or a break character is detected. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the FECF bit in the USART_ICR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">When transmitting data in smartcard mode, this bit is set when the maximum number of transmit attempts is reached without success (the card NACKs the data frame).</p><p class="TableIndent">An interrupt is generated if EIE = 1 in the USART_CR3 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Framing error is detected</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Framing error or break character is detected</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PE</span>: Parity error</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware when a parity error occurs in receiver mode. It is cleared by software, writing 1 to the PECF in the USART_ICR register. <br/>An interrupt is generated if PEIE = 1 in the USART_CR1 register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No parity error</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Parity error</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.11 USART interrupt flag clear register (USART\_ICR)

Address offset: 0x20

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.54px"/><col width="495.86px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WUCF</span>: Wake-up from low-power mode clear flag </p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the WUF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the wake-up from Stop feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. <span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 10.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a></span><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">.</span></p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMCF</span>: Character match clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the CMF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDRCF</span>:SPI slave underrun clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the UDRF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support SPI slave mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a></p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EOBCF</span>: End of block clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the EOBF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support smartcard mode, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RTOCF</span>: Receiver timeout clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the RTOF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the USART does not support the Receiver timeout feature, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CTSCF</span>: CTS clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the CTSIF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If the hardware flow control feature is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LBDCF</span>: LIN break detection clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the LBDF flag in the USART_ISR register.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>If LIN mode is not supported, this bit is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCBGTCF</span>: Transmission complete before Guard time clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the TCBGT flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCCF</span>: Transmission complete clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the TC flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TXFECF</span>: TXFIFO empty clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the TXFE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDLECF</span>: Idle line detected clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the IDLE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ORECF</span>: Overrun error clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the ORE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">NECF</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Noise detected clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the NE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FECF</span>: Framing error clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the FE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PECF</span>: Parity error clear flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Writing 1 to this bit clears the PE flag in the USART_ISR register.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.12 USART receive data register (USART\_RDR)

Address offset: 0x24

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.81px"/><col width="494.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 8:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RDR[8:0]</span>: Receive data value</p><p class="TableIndent">Contains the received data character.</p><p class="TableIndent">The RDR register provides the parallel interface between the input shift register and the internal bus (see <a href="#XREF_72145__Figure_1__USART_block_diagram24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 564</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent">When receiving with the parity enabled, the value read in the MSB bit is the received parity bit.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.81px"/><col width="494.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="133.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 8:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDR[8:0]</span>: Transmit data value</p><p class="TableIndent">Contains the data character to be transmitted.</p><p class="TableIndent">The USART_TDR register provides the parallel interface between the internal bus and the output shift register (see <a href="#XREF_72145__Figure_1__USART_block_diagram24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 564</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent">When transmitting with the parity enabled (PCE bit set to 1 in the USART_CR1 register), the value written in the MSB (bit 7 or bit 8 depending on the data length) has no effect because it is replaced by the parity.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This register must be written only when TXE/TXFNF<span style="font-style:normal;"> = </span>1.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 40.8.14 USART prescaler register (USART\_PRESC)

This register can only be written when the USART is disabled (UE = 0).

Address offset: 0x2C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.81px"/><col width="494.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="313.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PRESCALER[3:0]</span>: Clock prescaler</p><p class="TableBodyL">The USART input clock can be divided by a prescaler factor:</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: input clock not divided</p><p class="TableIndent">0001: input clock divided by 2</p><p class="TableIndent">0010: input clock divided by 4</p><p class="TableIndent">0011: input clock divided by 6</p><p class="TableIndent">0100: input clock divided by 8</p><p class="TableIndent">0101: input clock divided by 10</p><p class="TableIndent">0110: input clock divided by 12</p><p class="TableIndent">0111: input clock divided by 16</p><p class="TableIndent">1000: input clock divided by 32</p><p class="TableIndent">1001: input clock divided by 64</p><p class="TableIndent">1010: input clock divided by 128</p><p class="TableIndent">1011: input clock divided by 256</p><p class="TableIndent">Remaining combinations: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>When PRESCALER is programmed with a value different of the allowed ones, programmed prescaler value is 1011 i.e. input clock divided by 256.</p><p class="RegTNote_">If the prescaler is not supported, this bitfield is reserved and must be kept at reset value. Refer to <a href="#XREF_81814__17_2_General_description24" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 40.4: USART implementation on page 1691</a>.</p></td></tr></table></div>
